description: Documentation: update squads/example.yaml with the explicit Azure-DevOps-is-SCM-only note and the per-repo issue_provider override example, and document the dev onboarding flow (install app -> add squad yamls locally to ~/.kiro/crew/crons/squads/) plus the new squads_dir deployment config field in config.example.yaml (and README/steering if warranted). All prose in Portuguese to match the codebase.
steps: Edit squads/example.yaml: near issue_provider, add an explicit comment (pt-BR) 'Azure DevOps: apenas SCM (repos[].url), NUNCA issue_provider. Providers de issue suportados: github | jira.'

In squads/example.yaml under the `repos:` block, add a commented example showing a per-repo issue_provider override — mirroring the issue's example: squad default issue_provider: jira, one repo `https://github.com/eliasrosa/kirocrew-flow` with `issue_provider: github  # override: este repo usa GitHub Issues`, and an Azure DevOps repo entry that inherits jira (no issue_provider). Explain precedence (override por-repo > default da squad) in a comment.

Edit config.example.yaml: document the new `squads_dir` field for the deployment config — a DIRECTORY of squad yaml files (not a single file), e.g. `# squads_dir: ~/.kiro/crew/crons/squads/`. Explain relationship to `squad_config`: squads_dir is the recommended pattern for the installed app; squad_config (single file) remains supported as fallback/compat. Note that the squads directory lives in the INSTALLED APP, not inside the squad repo.

Add an onboarding section (pt-BR) describing the dev flow: install the app -> the app ships an empty squads dir (ex: ~/.kiro/crew/crons/squads/) -> dev drops one squad yaml per squad/project there -> the engine auto-loads all via load_squads_dir. Put this where it fits best: a short block in config.example.yaml comments and, if there is a natural home, a note in README.md or docs/ (e.g. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Do not duplicate large content — one authoritative place plus a pointer.

If any behavioral docs in README.md or .kiro/steering/*.md describe squad_config as the only mechanism, update them to mention squads_dir and per-repo issue_provider (only if such references exist — search first with grep).
Re-run `.venv/bin/pytest -q` to confirm docs edits did not break example-yaml-parsing tests (some tests load squads/example.yaml).
acceptance_criteria: squads/example.yaml contains the explicit comment that Azure DevOps is SCM-only and never an issue_provider, and lists github|jira as the supported issue providers.
squads/example.yaml shows a per-repo issue_provider override example matching the issue (github override on the flow repo, ADO repo inheriting jira).
config.example.yaml documents squads_dir as a directory with squad_config kept as fallback, and notes the squads dir lives in the installed app.
The dev onboarding flow (install -> add squad yamls -> auto-load) is documented in pt-BR in an authoritative place.
verification: .venv/bin/pytest -q stays green (example.yaml still parses under both PyYAML and mini_yaml where tested)
grep confirms the required strings exist in squads/example.yaml and config.example.yaml
findings: Docs-only change, no source logic touched. Edited squads/example.yaml (Azure-DevOps-is-SCM-only note near issue_provider + commented per-repo issue_provider override example: default jira, github override on eliasrosa/kirocrew-flow, ADO repo inheriting jira; precedence noted). Edited config.example.yaml (squads_dir directory field with precedence squads_dir > squad_config > inline, squad_config kept as fallback/compat, squads dir lives in installed app, pt-BR onboarding section). Added two short pointer blocks in README.md (squads_dir + per-repo issue_provider) pointing to config.example.yaml as authoritative; no steering edits needed (arquitetura.md's squad_config reference is a code-path narration, not the config mechanism). Verified squads/example.yaml still parses under BOTH PyYAML and forced _mini_yaml fallback (kept override illustration in comments to avoid fallback-parsing risk). Test suite: 1094 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed — the 1 failure is the known pre-existing chmod-as-root test test_prompts_loader.py::TestRenderPromptFallback::test_template_corrompido_ilegivel_usa_fallback (unrelated). Baseline preserved.
